articles.summary: Laser processing of silicon has long since become a standard method for wafer dicing, surface texturing, recrystallization after ion implantation, as well as surface amorphization, to name a few examples. Here, we introduce a different concept: the fabrication of vibrating microcavities in a commercial platform, Si wafers covered by a thick SiO2 layer, acting as a membrane. We demonstrate that by exposing our material system to single ultrashort laser pulses above the evaporation threshold of Si, a controlled delamination of the cover layer without fracture can be achieved, leading to the formation of a microcavity accompanied by a surface bulging up to 1.5 μm. …

We show here that laser irradiation in a plane is a way to induce and control such space charge at any depth in KTP single crystals. To this aim, we used a 1064 nm laser of average power less than 400 mW and with a repetition rate of 1 MHz leading to a pulse energy below 400 nJ. …

This approach produces well-confined ablation features with diameters of 5 μm to 10 μm. …

Herein, we propose a scalable method combining spatial beam shaping with orthogonal scanning via femtosecond laser to fabricate sub-wavelength structures (laser-induced periodic surface structures, LIPSS) on diamond for infrared antireflective windows. …

articles.summary: This study investigates the influence of laser pulse width, from femtoseconds (fs) to nanoseconds (ns), and gigahertz (GHz)-bursts on the ablation of graphite electrodes. GHz-burst laser ablation with burst widths of 50–100 ns showed the highest ablation efficiency and aspect ratio compared to fs and ns laser ablation. Analyses via scanning electron microscopy, light microscopy, and Raman spectroscopy revealed slight material modifications near ablated regions. The insights from the ablation study were transferred to theoretical considerations of potential process upscaling and reachable processing speeds as a function of the targeted structure pitch and ablation depth for a line pattern. …

Moreover, dissociation of two disulfide bonds together with backbone bonds has only been reported once, for insulin. In this study, we present evidence for the cleavage of not only one or two intricate disulfide bonds, but also for cleavage of backbone bonds of a multiply‐protonated sub‐sequence of the fibronectin protein. …

In this study, we introduce a novel six-dimensional (6D) multiplexing approach that exploits ultrafast interactions of polarized light with a three-dimensional medium. …

The resulting helical setting of 498 kHz, 15 W, 203 mm/s and 50 scans gave a mean taper of 0.90°. …

Although mechanical sawing remains the most widely used technique, it becomes inefficient for thicker wafers and induces numerous defects along the cut edges. Laser stealth dicing (SD) has emerged as a promising solution for the singulation of advanced semiconductor packages; however, current industrial implementations mainly rely on 1–2 μm infrared sources. In this work, we investigate the potential of a 2.8 μm nanosecond laser for SD of thick silicon wafers. Experiments are performed on boron-doped 〈100〉 silicon wafers of 650 μm thickness using a 60 ns mid-infrared source. …

Existing approaches are compared across process modelling, parameter optimisation, monitoring and intelligent control, while distinguishing nominal process inputs from physically meaningful descriptors and hybrid physics–ML methods. …
